response:
The manuscript titled "Known phyla, unknown proteome: a controlled census of the Rub' al-Khali soil metagenome" presents a metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) and protein catalogue reconstructed from 551 soil metagenomes collected across 62 sites and five expeditions in the Rub' al-Khali desert. From 14,426 quality-filtered bins, the authors dereplicate 5,438 species-level representatives (5,094 bacterial and 344 archaeal) and cluster 70,564,625 predicted coding sequences into 43,423,322 sequence clusters, of which 4,292,446 (9.89%) have no UniRef50 match at E <= 1e-3. To separate genuine unannotated coding sequences from gene-calling and assembly artefacts, the authors apply a five-criterion admission gate (yielding 106,042 recurrent multi-species dark families), compare 22 species-matched MAGs against long-read assemblies of 110 autochthonous desert isolates at the protein and nucleotide levels, model how genome-level dark fractions depend on taxonomy, assembly fragmentation and coding density, fold 2,838 confidence-qualified dark family representatives with ESMFold against 3,013 matched PDB controls, and benchmark catalogue novelty against MGnify, GEM, SPIRE and global desert soil datasets. Compared with earlier versions, the manuscript is substantially more rigorous: headline claims are appropriately scoped to conditional populations, technical confounders are treated as primary hypotheses rather than afterthoughts, and the distinction between taxonomic familiarity (all 5,438 representatives assign to known GTDB release 232 phyla) and gene-level novelty is clearly articulated. Regarding suitability for Nature Communications, the scale of the hyperarid soil sampling, the pairing of metagenomic bins with 110 long-read isolate genomes from the same soils, and the systematic decomposition of metagenomic "dark matter" into caller divergence, fragmentation, lineage effects and structural novelty provide a strong, generalizable resource and methodological template for environmental genomics. Several statistical and interpretive issues in the structural control baseline, the Pfam domain analysis, the breadth-of-coverage persistence metric, contaminant reporting, and internal cross-references should be resolved, and incorporating the strongest of the newly executed Round 5 control analyses will materially sharpen the paper.

Comments:

1. In Section 2.5 ("A subset of confident dark models lacks close reference folds"), the manuscript benchmarks the 2,838 confidence-qualified dark ESMFold models against 3,013 confidence-qualified PDB controls, stating at lines 318 to 322 of reviews/darkmatter-2026-10-13/round5/baseline_main.tex: "Of the 2,838 confidence-qualified dark models, 1,031 (36.3%) fall below a query-normalised TM-score of 0.5, compared with 101 of 3,013 controls (3.35%; Fig. \ref{fig:structural}a)." Lines 326 to 328 then add: "Under alignment-length normalisation, which does not penalise unaligned query extensions, 95 of the 2,838 dark models (3.35%) and 68 of the 3,013 controls (2.26%) fall below 0.5." While Methods lines 706 to 708 note that the 3,684 initial controls were "matched to an earlier candidate set by length and taxonomy", the manuscript does not disclose that after applying the pLDDT >= 0.70 gate, the 3,013 surviving controls have substantially higher model confidence than the 2,838 dark models (mean pLDDT 0.867 versus 0.775; 70% of dark candidates lie in the 0.70 to 0.80 pLDDT bins compared with 15% of controls, as documented in reproducibility/darkmatter/upstream_code/04_structure/00_structure_clean/README.md). Because the control failure rate is strongly pLDDT-dependent (5.49% in pLDDT 0.70 to 0.75 versus 1.53% above 0.90), the unadjusted 3.35% control floor is confounded by model confidence. The authors' own stratified reweighting in reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/04_structure/00_structure_clean/05_validate/stratified_floor.tsv shows that after reweighting controls to the candidate pLDDT x length distribution, the query-normalised control floor rises from 3.35% to 4.49% (reducing the excess multiplier from 10.84x to 8.09x, 95% bootstrap CI 5.96 to 11.49), whereas under alignment-length normalisation the reweighted control floor is 2.43% against 3.35% in candidates (multiplier 1.38x, 95% CI 0.875 to 2.407, crossing 1.0). The main text should report the pLDDT x length-adjusted control floors and confidence intervals alongside the unadjusted rates, and explicitly note that under alignment-length normalisation the excess of dark models below TM = 0.5 is not statistically distinguishable from the pLDDT-matched control floor.

2. Relatedly, the Pfam domain comparison at lines 345 to 350 of baseline_main.tex ("Pfam recognises a domain in 8.75% of the 4,880 member proteins of the 1,031 families and in 14.0% of those families, compared with 90.7% of the controls") is incomplete in two ways that are already resolved in the upstream tables under reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/04_structure/pfam_candidates_clean/results/{set_summary.tsv,duf_share.tsv}. First, among the 427 Pfam-positive member proteins in the 1,031 low-qTM families, 124 (29.0%) hit exclusively DUF/UPF domains of unknown function (leaving 303/4,880, or 6.21%, with any named functional domain, versus 90.34% in controls), and 382 of the 427 (89.5%) still contain a contiguous uncovered region of at least 80 residues (median Pfam sequence coverage 25.3% and median longest uncovered stretch 159 residues, compared with 88.5% coverage and 22 residues in controls). Second, the like-for-like dark comparator set (QnotK_reps, the 1,807 confident dark models that did match a reference fold at qTM >= 0.5) has an even lower Pfam hit rate (5.59%, 101/1,807; 4.21% with any named domain) and shorter protein length (median 193 residues versus 265 residues in the 1,031 qTM < 0.5 representatives), with median Pfam coverage of 55.9% when a domain is present. Reporting QnotK_reps alongside the PDB controls is essential because it shows that Pfam absence is a general property of sequence-dark proteins (which are UniRef50-negative by definition), whereas what distinguishes the qTM < 0.5 subset from the qTM >= 0.5 dark subset is longer polypeptide length and large unaligned or uncovered regions (median 164 residues in K_reps_only versus 65 residues in QnotK_reps).

3. In Section 2.2 ("Recurrent dark families show purifying selection and expression") and Section 2.6 ("Reference bias and global desert comparisons"), sample and site occupancy of the 106,042 admitted dark families are defined using a breadth-of-coverage threshold of at least 50% (cf50). At lines 145 to 149 of baseline_main.tex, the manuscript reports: "Under a presence rule of at least 50% breadth of coverage, 79.4% of the 106,042 admitted families were detected in all five expeditions and 94.8% in at least four; only four families were restricted to a single sample. A prevalence-conditioned null and competitive mapping would be needed to interpret temporal persistence beyond repeated DNA detection." Beyond the lack of a permutation null in the baseline text (which is addressed by the Round 5 H2 extension), the cf50 rule introduces a strong mechanical length bias that is documented in reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/06_darkmatter/specificity_clean/results/{presence_rule_length_test.tsv,s14_persistence_by_length.tsv,b6_length_confound_with_smag.tsv} but omitted from Section 2.2. Because a single 150-bp read covers at least 50% of any gene up to 300 bp (100 residues) whereas longer genes require multiple dispersed reads to reach 50% breadth, apparent sample occupancy and five-expedition detection under cf50 decline monotonically with protein length: five-expedition detection is 89.7% for families under 60 residues (n = 24,535; median 201 samples) and 81.9% for 60 to 99 residues (n = 26,099; median 107 samples), versus 67.1% for families of at least 250 residues (n = 14,387; median 55 samples). In presence_rule_length_test.tsv, the highest site-occupancy bin (90 to 100% of sites) under cf50 has a median protein length of 25 residues (98.7% under 100 residues), whereas under a read-count rule (tpm_any) the length gradient reverses (median length rises from 76 residues in the 0 to 5% occupancy bin to 175 residues in the 90 to 100% bin). Section 2.2 should explicitly report how the 79.4% five-expedition figure stratifies by protein length (for example, <100 residues versus >=100 residues) and note the interaction between 150-bp read length and the 50% breadth threshold.

4. In Section 2.3 ("Cultured desert isolates capture a biased subset of the metagenome"), lines 217 to 222 of baseline_main.tex state: "Among DNA-supported calls, 344 of 735 dark calls (46.8%) and 592 of 67,802 annotated calls (0.87%) had no culture CDS overlapping at least 50% of the aligned span (complete genes of at least 100 residues: 19/59, 32.2%, versus 456/57,806, 0.79%). Because the two assemblies used different callers (pyrodigal on MAGs, Bakta on cultures), these percentages combine caller threshold differences with local assembly context." In the baseline manuscript, this critical question (how much of the 46.8% annotation gap is caused by Bakta versus Pyrodigal caller parameterization as opposed to MAG fragmentation and local sequence divergence) is left unresolved. The authors have now executed the controlled caller-substitution experiment in reproducibility/darkmatter/round5_extensions/scripts/culture_caller.py (running pyrodigal v3.7.1 -p meta --no-stop-codon on the 22 culture assemblies). Integrating this result directly into Section 2.3 will substantially strengthen the paper, provided the authors report both the pooled reduction (344/735, 46.8%, down to 235/735, 32.0%, at >=50% span; 19/59, 32.2%, down to 17/59, 28.8%, for complete genes >=100 residues) and two critical nuances visible in the per-pair and subset tables (reproducibility/darkmatter/round5_extensions/results/culture_caller/{summary.tsv,per_pair.tsv}): (i) the caller rescue is highly concentrated across pairs, with 11 of the 22 pairs showing zero net change, a single pair (30PRr3__single_SemiBin_149) contributing 44 of the 118 gained calls (37.3%), and the top three pairs contributing 67 of 118 (56.8%) (per-pair median missing-CDS fraction 44.2% under Bakta versus 36.4% under Pyrodigal, paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0033); and (ii) among the 42 DNA-supported dark calls belonging to the 47 admitted recurrent families, caller substitution produces zero net reduction (18/42, or 42.9%, lack a culture CDS under both Bakta and Pyrodigal, with 1 gained and 1 lost).

5. Contaminant reporting and sensitivity checks are currently inconsistent across Results, Discussion and Methods. In Methods lines 550 to 556, the manuscript reports that two species representatives accounted for 100% of assigned reads in the no-template extraction control (SNTC; 4.30% and 4.26% relative abundance, inverse DNA concentration correlations rho = -0.490 and -0.469 across 550 soil samples) and that ten representatives carried contigs aligning to the SNTC cloning vector. However, Results (lines 195 to 196) and Methods (lines 628 to 630) name only the Escherichia coli representative (V42PRr2__single_SemiBin_33) and never identify the second SNTC read-mapped contaminant, which reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/06_darkmatter/contamination_clean/results/control_profiles.tsv shows is Cutibacterium acnes (51Dr3__single_SemiBin_390, accounting for 49.8% of mapped SNTC reads and detected in 290/550 soil samples). Furthermore, Discussion lines 410 to 413 state: "Twelve catalogue representatives showed read or contig matches to the negative extraction control, and the Escherichia coli representative was excluded from the culture comparison, but the catalogue-level lineage and environmental summaries still include the flagged representatives. Sensitivity analyses across these summaries are required to assess their contribution." Leaving a statement in the Discussion that sensitivity analyses "are required" is unnecessary when the exact numbers are already available in reproducibility/darkmatter/inputs/06_darkmatter/lineage_darkness_clean/results/v2_reps.tsv.gz and reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/06_darkmatter/contamination_clean/results/control_contig_hits.tsv: the two SNTC read-mapped representatives carry 6,401 proteins and only 54 dark proteins (6 on E. coli and 48 on C. acnes), and the ten SNTC vector-matching representatives carry 36,430 proteins and 1,738 dark proteins. Combined, all 12 SNTC-flagged representatives account for 42,831 of 20,379,930 representative proteins (0.21%) and 1,792 of 1,600,067 representative dark proteins (0.11%). The authors should explicitly name Cutibacterium acnes (51Dr3__single_SemiBin_390) and Mixta alhagi (T5PRr1__self_SemiBin_614, 3,171/3,173 bp vector match at 99.94% identity) in Methods Section 4.2, and replace the open-ended caveat at lines 410 to 413 with the exact protein and dark-protein counts carried by the 12 flagged bins.

6. The manuscript contains unresolved cross-references to tables that do not exist in reviews/darkmatter-2026-10-13/round5/baseline_main.tex and a species-count discrepancy between Results and Discussion:
- Line 779 (Methods Section 4.10) cites "compatible-solute synthesis panel (Supplementary Table~S3)", and lines 855 to 856 (Supplementary Note S1) cite "The annotated fraction of the catalogue carries the toolkit expected of a hyperarid soil (Extended Data Table 1)." Neither Supplementary Table S3 nor Extended Data Table 1 is present or defined anywhere in baseline_main.tex (Note: reviews/darkmatter-2026-10-13/round4/response.md incorrectly stated that these strings did not occur in the manuscript).
- Line 438 (Discussion) states: "The two archaeal classes are culture and fold targets, and none of the 24 shared species remaining after contaminant exclusion already in hand as strains is archaeal." Earlier, Results lines 194 to 196 state: "They shared a species-level ANI match with 25 catalogue representatives, yielding 23 representative--culture groups after assignment to the best-ANI representative. Excluding the Escherichia coli representative detected in the no-template control left 22 groups." Switching between "22 groups" in Results and "24 shared species" in Discussion without noting that 25 initial ANI matches minus 1 contaminant equals 24 matched representatives before best-ANI collapsing (22 after collapsing) is confusing and should be harmonized.

Minor:

- In Section 2.6 (line 366 of baseline_main.tex), the text reports "8,857 shared KEGG orthologues" for the 448-sample paired 16S/MAG comparison, whereas reproducibility/darkmatter/round5_extensions/scripts/profile_extensions.py and results/profile_summary.json report 8,860 shared KOs in the common universe (because 3 KOs in the 8,860-KO intersection are all-zero in the MAG table across the 448-sample cohort, leaving 8,857 detected in both). Please harmonize this count or state the 3 all-zero KOs explicitly in Methods Section 4.9.
- In baseline_references.bib, seven cited published journal articles have incomplete bibliographic metadata (missing volume and page/article numbers): chan2021trnascan (Nucleic Acids Research, 2021, 49, W297-W303), eberhardt2012antifam (Database, 2012, 2012, bas003), mugal2014time (Molecular Biology and Evolution, 2014, 31, 212-231), nelson2020olgenie (Molecular Biology and Evolution, 2020, 37, 2440-2452), orr2026spurious (Frontiers in Bioinformatics, 2026), shaw2023skani (Nature Methods, 2023, 20, 1661-1665), and yooseph2007gos (PLOS Biology, 2007, 5, e16). In addition, chan2021trnascan at line 1332 of baseline_references.bib contains literal non-breaking space characters (\u00a0) in author initials, and seven entries use truncated "and others" author lists in the BibTeX source (blin2025antismash8, bowers2017mimag, harris2020numpy, maestre2015aridity, nayfach2021gem, richardson2023mgnify, virtanen2020scipy).
- In reproducibility/darkmatter/round5_extensions/scripts/culture_caller.py (and its output results/culture_caller/per_gene.tsv.gz), the Prodigal partiality flag ("00", "01", "10", "11") is written without quoting and read back by pandas without dtype={"partial": str}, which silently coerces "00" and "01" to integers 0 and 1 if downstream scripts do not force string typing. Note that culture_caller.py line 161 handles this defensively via str(val).zfill(2), but pinning dtype={"partial": str} when reading per_gene.tsv.gz is safer.
- In Figure 1 (baseline_main.pdf p. 25) and Figure 3 (p. 27), the visual layout is clean and legible; the three pdf_integrity.txt text-contrast alerts on p. 25 ("69", "90", "61") correspond to legitimate white-on-dark-blue numeric cell labels in the Figure 1b missing-rank matrix and pose no integrity issue.


Extensions:

Part I: Assessment of the Three Completed Round 5 Extensions (reproducibility/darkmatter/round5_extensions/)

1. Extension H1: Controlled gene-caller substitution on the 22 representative-culture pairs (reproducibility/darkmatter/round5_extensions/scripts/culture_caller.py; results/culture_caller/{summary.tsv,per_pair.tsv,per_gene.tsv.gz,run.json})
- Recommendation: INCLUDE IN MAIN TEXT (Section 2.3 and Methods Section 4.4) AND SUPPLEMENTARY TABLE (per_pair.tsv and summary.tsv).
- Estimand and conditional scope: Among the 735 dark and 67,802 annotated MAG genes that align at the nucleotide level (>=80% query coverage, >=70% nucleotide identity) to a species-matched long-read culture assembly across the 22 contaminant-excluded representative-culture pairs, H1 estimates the change in the proportion of aligned MAG genes lacking a same-strand culture CDS across >=50% (and >=90%) of the aligned span when the culture assembly is re-called with the exact MAG gene caller (pyrodigal v3.7.1 -p meta --no-stop-codon) in place of Bakta v1.11.4.
- Effect size and mechanistic value: At the >=50% overlap threshold, replacing Bakta with Pyrodigal reduces the missing-CDS rate for DNA-supported dark calls from 344/735 (46.8%) to 235/735 (32.0%), a net reduction of 109 genes (14.8 percentage points; 118 gained culture CDS overlaps, of which 116 are in-frame compatible; 9 lost). At the >=90% overlap threshold, the missing-CDS rate drops from 400/735 (54.4%) to 281/735 (38.2%). Crucially, stratifying by reciprocal-protein sharing (by joining results/culture_caller/per_gene.tsv.gz with culture_nucleotide_cigar/per_gene.tsv) shows that all 118 gained overlaps at >=50% span occur in the 516 protein-unshared dark calls (where no_major_CDS_overlap drops from 343/516, 66.5%, to 226/516, 43.8%, and in_frame_compatible rises from 151/516, 29.3%, to 267/516, 51.7%), whereas 8 of the 9 lost overlaps occur in the 219 protein-shared dark calls (1/219 to 9/219). Furthermore, stratifying by Prodigal completeness flag shows that 117 of the 118 rescued dark calls are complete internal ORFs (partial == "00", median length 49.5 residues; missing-CDS rate drops from 295/570, 51.8%, to 187/570, 32.8%), whereas partial contig-edge ORFs (partial != "00", n = 165) show virtually no change (49/165, 29.7%, to 48/165, 29.1%).
- Dependence and subset caveats that must be reported:
  (a) Pair-level clustering: Because genes are nested within 22 genome pairs, pooling 735 genes treats co-located calls on the same MAG as independent. Inspection of results/culture_caller/per_pair.tsv reveals extreme concentration across pairs: 11 of the 22 pairs (50%) exhibit zero net change in dark missing-CDS counts; a single pair (30PRr3__single_SemiBin_149, paired with 33D4_2) accounts for 44 of the 118 gained dark CDS calls (37.3%), and the top three pairs (30PRr3__single_SemiBin_149, 25Dr2__self_SemiBin_74, and F21Sr2__single_SemiBin_43) account for 67 of 118 (56.8%). Across the 22 pairs, the per-pair median missing-CDS rate drops from 44.2% (IQR 35.7% to 56.0%) under Bakta to 36.4% (IQR 23.0% to 41.7%) under Pyrodigal (median per-pair delta -3.6 percentage points; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.0033). Both the pooled counts and the per-pair median/IQR should be reported.
  (b) Admitted recurrent families: Among the 42 DNA-supported dark calls that belong to the 47 admitted recurrent dark families (spanning 10 pairs), caller substitution produces zero net change: 18/42 (42.9%) lack a culture CDS under Bakta and 18/42 (42.9%) lack a culture CDS under Pyrodigal (1 gained, 1 lost) at both the 50% and 90% overlap thresholds.
  (c) Residual non-caller gap: Even when the exact same Pyrodigal command is run on both assemblies, 235/735 (32.0%) of DNA-supported dark calls (and 17/59, 28.8%, of complete dark calls >=100 residues) still have no culture CDS, compared with 498/67,802 (0.73%) of annotated calls. This proves that caller choice (Bakta versus Pyrodigal) accounts for roughly one-third of the apparent annotation discrepancy, while the remaining two-thirds reflect sequence divergence between conspecific strains (95 to 99% ANI altering start/stop codons) and Prodigal meta-mode dynamic programming differences between fragmented MAG contigs and intact long-read chromosomes.

2. Extension H2: Stratified permutation null for five-expedition detection (reproducibility/darkmatter/round5_extensions/scripts/profile_extensions.py; results/{temporal_summary.tsv,temporal_design.json,temporal_per_family.tsv.gz})
- Recommendation: INCLUDE AS A ONE-SENTENCE QUALIFICATION IN MAIN TEXT (Section 2.2, lines 145 to 149) WITH FULL TABLE IN SUPPLEMENT.
- Estimand and sampling null: For the 106,042 admitted dark families across the 551 soil metagenomes (550 with expedition metadata across 5 trips), H2 tests whether the observed fraction of families detected (at >=50% breadth of coverage) in all five expeditions (79.38%, 84,180/106,042) exceeds the expectation under random permutation of expedition labels within site x soil-position strata (159 strata total; 121 multi-trip strata containing 509 exchangeable samples; 499 permutations).
- Assessment of result and why observed is below null: Under the site x compartment permutation null, the expected all-five-expedition detection rate is 82.74% (95% permutation interval 81.12% to 84.19%), which is 3.36 percentage points higher than the observed 79.38% (one-sided p_lower = 0.002; p_upper = 1.000). The deficit of observed relative to null holds in every sample-occupancy bin, peaking at -10.28 percentage points in the 10 to 24 sample bin (2.51% observed versus 12.78% null) and -6.26 percentage points in the 25 to 49 sample bin (33.54% observed versus 39.80% null). Why is the observed multi-trip persistence lower than the stratified permutation null? First, permuting sample labels at the individual sample level within a site x compartment stratum breaks up co-located biological replicate triples (r1, r2, r3) collected during the same expedition visit. In the real data, detections are positively correlated within replicate triples of a single visit; permuting individual sample labels across visits scatters those replicate detections across different trips, mechanically inflating the number of distinct expeditions hit under the null. Second, because Expedition 2 (March 2022) sampled only 7 sites (37 samples across 17 site x compartment blocks containing 127 total samples), any family with zero detections inside those 127 samples can never be detected in all 5 trips under any within-block permutation (11,276 families, or 10.6%, have null_all_five_count == 0), and any family with dense occupancy in those blocks is detected in all 5 trips in every permutation (62,280 families, or 58.7%, have null_all_five_count == 499), leaving only 32,486 families (30.6%) variable across permutations.
- Scientific value for the manuscript: Despite the replicate-clustering nuance, H2 provides a clean, decisive answer to the caveat already written at lines 148 to 149 of baseline_main.tex ("A prevalence-conditioned null and competitive mapping would be needed to interpret temporal persistence beyond repeated DNA detection"): the 79.4% five-expedition detection rate does not exceed what is expected from spatial prevalence and revisit geometry alone (79.4% observed versus 82.7% under site x compartment label permutation), and instead reflects broad spatial occupancy combined with within-visit replicate clustering. Replacing the speculative caveat at lines 148 to 149 with this exact result tightens Section 2.2.

3. Extension H3: Paired 16S-PICRUSt2 versus MAG functional-profile permutation nulls and abundance-threshold sensitivity (reproducibility/darkmatter/round5_extensions/scripts/profile_extensions.py; results/{profile_summary.json,profile_thresholds_summary.tsv,profile_pairwise_rank_correlations.tsv.gz})
- Recommendation: INCLUDE IN SUPPLEMENT ONLY (or at most a brief parenthetical in Section 2.6, lines 363 to 370), AND OMIT THE DEGENERATE 1e-3 THRESHOLD ROW.
- Estimand and critical evaluation: Across the 448 soil samples with paired 16S amplicon and shotgun MAG profiles, H3 evaluates (a) whether the mean paired Spearman rank correlation across the 8,860 common KOs (mean 0.8431, median 0.8442) exceeds block-permuted nulls within trip x compartment (448 exchangeable samples across 14 blocks; null mean 0.8245, delta = +0.0185, p = 0.0002) and within trip x compartment x site (146 exchangeable samples across 66 blocks; null mean 0.8408, delta = +0.0023, p = 0.0002), and (b) how binary KO presence/absence agreement (Jaccard, recall, precision) varies across relative-abundance thresholds from 0 to 1e-3.
- Why H3 belongs in the supplement rather than the main text:
  (a) In the sampling design, a trip x compartment x site block consists of co-located biological replicate soil cores (r1, r2, r3) collected at the same site, in the same soil position, on the same day. Therefore, permuting within trip x compartment x site (delta = +0.0023) tests within-visit replicate variability rather than site-specific functional tracking. Using the full 448 x 448 correlation matrix in results/profile_pairwise_rank_correlations.tsv.gz, we verified that the grand mean correlation across all 200,256 off-diagonal unpaired sample pairs catalogue-wide is already 0.8215, that permuting across trips within site x compartment (406 exchangeable samples in 111 blocks) gives null mean 0.8334 (delta = +0.0101), and that a sample's own PICRUSt2 profile is its top-1 highest-correlating match in only 32 of 448 samples (7.1%, median rank 77.5 out of 448). This confirms the statement already present at lines 368 to 370 of baseline_main.tex: the high baseline correlation (~0.82 to 0.84) is dominated by conserved desert-wide housekeeping KO copy-number hierarchy, with a modest but statistically significant sample- and site-specific increment (+0.010 to +0.022).
  (b) In the threshold sensitivity table (results/profile_thresholds_summary.tsv), mild filtering at relative abundance > 1e-6 or > 1e-5 usefully demonstrates that removing low-abundance PICRUSt2 tail predictions reduces predicted KOs per sample from median 10,543 (unfiltered) to 6,547.5 (at 1e-6) and 4,932.5 (at 1e-5), raising median Jaccard overlap with MAG KOs from 0.634 to 0.697 and 0.696. However, the 1e-3 threshold row in profile_thresholds_summary.tsv is a numerical artefact and must not be reported as a meaningful recall statistic: because total KO relative abundance is normalized across thousands of orthologues, 446 of the 448 MAG samples have zero KOs exceeding 1e-3 (median mag_kos = 0), so recall_of_mag is NaN for 446/448 samples and the reported median recall of 0.152 in profile_thresholds_summary.tsv is computed from only the 2 outlier samples that had non-zero MAG KOs at 1e-3.


Part II: Ranked Additional Falsifiable Hypotheses Using Existing IBEX and Local Data

The following four testable hypotheses do not repeat H1, H2 or H3, require no new wet-lab experiments, respect the strict separation from the companion phage (../empty-quarter-phages), amplicon (../empty-quarter-amplicon) and air (lifeonair/) manuscripts, and are ordered by scientific impact and immediate feasibility. All post hoc analyses are explicitly labelled as exploratory or sensitivity checks.

Hypothesis 1 (Rank 1, Feasible immediately from local tables; main-text upgrade for Section 2.5): Confidence- and length-stratified structural novelty floor and like-for-like Pfam domain architecture decomposition across dark and control fold sets.
- Exploratory/confirmatory status and companion-paper boundary: Methodological control and sensitivity analysis directly strengthening Section 2.5 (ESMFold structural census); zero overlap with phage, amplicon or air papers.
- Scientific question: Does the excess of low reference-similarity folds (TM < 0.5) among confidence-qualified dark proteins persist after controlling for the post-gate pLDDT and polypeptide-length mismatch between dark models (n = 2,838) and PDB controls (n = 3,013), and is the scarcity of Pfam domains in the 1,031 low-qTM families a specific signature of structural novelty or a general property of sequence-dark proteins combined with unaligned terminal/internal extensions?
- Why it adds substantive value: In the current manuscript, the headline structural comparison (36.3% versus 3.35% for qTM < 0.5; 3.35% versus 2.26% for alnTM < 0.5) is vulnerable to the criticism that the PDB controls have much higher pLDDT (mean 0.867 versus 0.775) and that Pfam scarcity (8.75% versus 90.7%) simply rediscovers that UniRef50-dark proteins lack sequence-database hits. Answering both questions with a stratified control floor and the internal dark comparator (QnotK_reps, n = 1,807) makes Section 2.5 rigorous.
- Actual available inputs (all verified locally):
  (1) reproducibility/darkmatter/inputs/04_structure/00_structure_clean/05_validate/per_rep_structures.tsv.gz (n = 2,838 dark representatives with length, plddt_mean, ptm, qtm, alntm, n_members);
  (2) reproducibility/darkmatter/inputs/04_structure/00_structure_clean/05_validate/per_control_structures.tsv.gz (n = 3,013 PDB controls with identical columns);
  (3) reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/04_structure/00_structure_clean/05_validate/stratified_floor.tsv;
  (4) reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/04_structure/pfam_candidates_clean/results/{set_summary.tsv,duf_share.tsv,length_matched_check.tsv}.
- Unit of replication and estimand: The unit of replication is the confidence-qualified protein model (2,838 dark family representatives, partitioned into 1,031 K_reps with qTM < 0.5 and 1,807 QnotK_reps with qTM >= 0.5, plus 3,013 PDB controls). The primary estimands are: (i) the direct standardization (reweighted) control failure rate and candidate-to-control risk ratio across joint pLDDT ([0.70, 0.75), [0.75, 0.80), [0.80, 0.85), [0.85, 0.90), [0.90, 1.00]) x length ([100, 150), [150, 200), [200, 300), [300, 500), [500, inf)) strata for both qTM < 0.5 and alnTM < 0.5, with 2,000-replicate nonparametric bootstrap 95% CIs; and (ii) the difference in Pfam domain hit rate, DUF-only share, covered sequence fraction, and maximum uncovered contiguous stretch (>=80 residues) across K_reps (n = 1,031; 4,880 members), QnotK_reps (n = 1,807), and PDB controls (n = 3,013).
- Controls and dependence structure: Family-level analysis (K_reps_only, n = 1,031, versus QnotK_reps, n = 1,807) avoids within-family dependence of the 4,880 member proteins; bootstrap resampling is performed at the family/control-protein level within pLDDT x length cells.
- Outcome interpretation (including informative negative result): As verified in audit_part2.json, for qTM < 0.5 the pLDDT x length-standardized control floor is 4.49%, yielding a robust 8.09-fold excess in dark candidates (95% CI 5.96 to 11.49; positive result confirming query-level structural divergence). Conversely, for alnTM < 0.5, the standardized control floor is 2.43% against 3.35% in dark candidates, yielding a risk ratio of 1.38 (95% CI 0.875 to 2.407), an informative negative result demonstrating that once local partial alignments are not penalized for unaligned query extensions, the rate of completely novel local folds is indistinguishable from the confidence-matched PDB baseline. Simultaneously, comparing K_reps (9.02% Pfam hit rate, median length 265 residues, median uncovered gap 164 residues) against QnotK_reps (5.59% Pfam hit rate, median length 193 residues, median uncovered gap 65 residues) proves that Pfam absence reflects sequence darkness generally, whereas qTM < 0.5 specifically captures longer dark proteins carrying large unannotated domains or extensions (>=80 residues in 89.2% of Pfam-positive K_reps).

Hypothesis 2 (Rank 2, Exploratory; feasible immediately from local tables; high biological value for Section 2.4): Core-divergence versus accessory-proteome expansion as the driver of extreme darkness in desert Thermoplasmatota (c__SW-10-69-26 versus c__E2).
- Exploratory/confirmatory status and companion-paper boundary: Exploratory post hoc comparative-genomic test within Section 2.4 (Lineage concentration of the dark proteome); uses only archaeal MAG representatives in this catalogue and has no overlap with phage, amplicon or air papers.
- Scientific question: Does the elevated dark-proteome fraction of desert Thermoplasmatota (median 31.1%, n = 237) reflect a simple "amino-acid divergence clock" (closer external reference genomes in GTDB/MGnify yielding lower dark fractions), or does it reflect lineage-specific accessory proteome expansion in class c__SW-10-69-26 (n = 185) relative to its sister desert class c__E2 (n = 51)?
- Why it adds substantive value: Section 2.4 establishes that Thermoplasmatota is the darkest phylum in the Rub' al-Khali catalogue (31.1% median dark fraction, persisting at +22.4 percentage points in matched bacterial pairs and +16.1 points against Patescibacteriota) and reports nearest-relative AAI (median 64.6%, range 48.7% to 84.7%). However, the manuscript currently stops at reporting the AAI range without testing whether AAI to external references actually predicts darkness within Thermoplasmatota, or why c__SW-10-69-26 (32.0% dark) is significantly darker than c__E2 (28.3% dark). Testing this distinguishes between two fundamental evolutionary mechanisms: uniform sequence divergence of a conserved proteome (under which dark fraction should correlate negatively with external AAI) versus proteome expansion via lineage-specific genes lacking external orthologues (under which external AAI of the shared core is decoupled from dark fraction, while genome size, total CDS count, and the non-RBH gene fraction drive darkness).
- Actual available inputs (all verified locally):
  (1) reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/06_darkmatter/lineage_darkness_clean/results/v2_thermo_relatives_pairs.tsv (n = 237 Thermoplasmatota representatives with cls, order_r232, family_r232, genus_r232, external best aai, aai_n_rbh, aai_frac_rbh, aai_desert);
  (2) reproducibility/darkmatter/inputs/06_darkmatter/lineage_darkness_clean/results/v2_reps.tsv.gz (completeness, contamination, length, N50, n_proteins, n_dark, dark_fraction).
- Unit of replication and estimand: The unit of replication is the dereplicated Thermoplasmatota species representative (n = 237; 185 c__SW-10-69-26, 51 c__E2, 1 c__Thermoplasmata). The estimands are: (i) the Spearman rank correlation (and OLS slope controlling for completeness and log10(N50)) between dark_fraction and best external AAI (aai) versus the fraction of genes with an external reciprocal best hit (aai_frac_rbh); and (ii) the nonparametric shift (Hodges-Lehmann median difference and Mann-Whitney U test) between c__SW-10-69-26 and c__E2 in genome size (Mb), total protein count, dark protein count, dark fraction, and external AAI.
- Controls and dependence structure: Control for assembly completeness, contamination, and log10(N50) via multiple regression, and check robustness at the genus/family cluster level (grouping by family_r232 / genus_r232) to account for phylogenetic non-independence among congeneric species representatives.
- Outcome interpretation (including informative negative result): Our audit check in audit_part3.json shows a striking double dissociation: first, external AAI has virtually zero correlation with dark fraction across the 237 Thermoplasmatota representatives (Spearman rho = 0.012, p = 0.85; genomes with genus-level external relatives at AAI >= 65%, n = 111, have median dark fraction 31.4% versus 30.7% for AAI < 65%, n = 126, an informative negative result that refutes a simple core amino-acid divergence clock). Second, c__SW-10-69-26 and c__E2 have virtually identical external AAI in their shared core (median 64.79% versus 64.19%, p = 0.048), yet c__SW-10-69-26 has a 40% larger genome (median 3.17 Mb, IQR 2.73 to 3.66 Mb, versus 2.26 Mb, IQR 2.15 to 2.55 Mb; p = 1.66e-16) and 1,018 more proteins per genome (median 3,460 versus 2,442 proteins, p = 4.15e-20; median 1,098 versus 693 dark proteins), with a 3.7 percentage-point higher dark fraction (32.0% versus 28.3%, p = 2.96e-11), and dark fraction correlates negatively with the external RBH gene fraction within c__SW-10-69-26 (rho = -0.301, p = 3.1e-5). Adding 3 to 4 sentences reporting this contrast in Section 2.4 provides a concrete evolutionary insight into why c__SW-10-69-26 dominates the archaeal dark proteome.

Hypothesis 3 (Rank 3, Feasible immediately from local tables; strengthens Section 2.6): Biome-matched soil MAG comparison (SMAG, 40,039 soil MAGs / 129.55M proteins, versus GEM, 52,515 multi-biome MAGs / 122.98M proteins) and explicit resolution of the cf50 length-occupancy confound.
- Exploratory/confirmatory status and companion-paper boundary: Methodological sensitivity analysis for Section 2.2 and Section 2.6; uses already-computed results in reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/06_darkmatter/specificity_clean/results/ and has no overlap with companion manuscripts.
- Scientific question: (a) When benchmarking the 106,042 Rub' al-Khali dark families and 106,042 matched annotated controls against external genome-resolved catalogues of nearly identical protein-sequence volume (~123M to 130M proteins), does a dedicated global soil MAG catalogue (SMAG, 129.55M proteins from 40,039 soil MAGs) recover substantially more desert dark families than a general multi-biome MAG catalogue (GEM, 122.98M proteins from 52,515 MAGs), and how much does adding SMAG reduce the apparent reference-unmatched fraction? (b) Does the higher site occupancy of externally matched versus unmatched dark families survive within narrow protein-length strata once the cf50 breadth-of-coverage length bias is controlled?
- Why it adds substantive value: In Section 2.6 (lines 370 to 388 of baseline_main.tex), the manuscript compares GEM (123M proteins, 4.9% hit rate for dark families), Global Deserts (15M proteins, 36.1% hit rate), MGnify90 (178M proteins, 61.9% hit rate) and SPIRE (535M proteins, 59.5% hit rate). A natural referee question is whether GEM performs poorly (4.9%) simply because it is non-soil-enriched, whereas SPIRE/MGnify succeed because they include soil metagenomes. The authors have already run the exact soil-specific genome-resolved control (SMAG, Ma et al. 2023, 40,039 soil MAGs, 129,550,340 proteins) in specificity_clean/results/{smag_content_vs_depth.tsv,union_specificity_with_smag_summary.tsv,b6_absence_occupancy_by_length_with_smag.tsv}, but have not yet reported it in baseline_main.tex.
- Actual available inputs (all verified locally):
  (1) reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/06_darkmatter/specificity_clean/results/smag_content_vs_depth.tsv;
  (2) reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/06_darkmatter/specificity_clean/results/union_specificity_with_smag_summary.tsv;
  (3) reproducibility/darkmatter/source_snapshot/06_darkmatter/specificity_clean/results/{b6_absence_occupancy_by_length_with_smag.tsv,s14_persistence_by_length.tsv,presence_rule_length_test.tsv}.
- Unit of replication and estimand: The unit of replication is the admitted protein family (106,042 dark families and 106,042 length- and size-matched annotated control families). The estimands are: (i) the difference in database hit rate between SMAG (129.55M soil MAG proteins) and GEM (122.98M multi-biome MAG proteins) relative to the MGnify90 random-subsampling size expectation; (ii) the reduction in the union-absent dark fraction when SMAG is added to known genome space (GEM + SPIRE -> GEM + SPIRE + SMAG) and to all named references (MGnify90 + GEM + Deserts + SPIRE + SMAG); and (iii) the difference in median site and sample occupancy between reference-absent and reference-present dark families within each of the five protein-length strata (<60, 60-99, 100-149, 150-249, >=250 residues).
- Controls and dependence structure: Matched annotated controls (106,042 families matched on representative length and cluster size) and MGnify90 subsampling curves provide both functional and database-volume baselines; stratifying occupancy by the five length bins controls for the mechanical coupling between gene length and >=50% breadth of coverage.
- Outcome interpretation (including informative negative result): At almost the exact same database size as GEM (129.55M versus 122.98M proteins), the soil-specific SMAG catalogue hits 40.47% of Rub' al-Khali dark families (and 98.43% of annotated controls) versus 4.93% in GEM, an 8.2-fold increase that directly quantifies the power of biome-matched soil genome catalogues, while still falling 27.69 percentage points below the MGnify90 size-matched expectation (68.16%) because SMAG lacks hyperarid desert representation. Adding SMAG reduces the fraction of dark families absent from genome-resolved catalogues (GEM + SPIRE) from 39.10% (41,460) to 33.53% (35,555) and reduces absence across all five resources combined from 28.74% (30,479) to 26.83% (28,446). Across length strata (b6_absence_occupancy_by_length_with_smag.tsv), reference-absent and reference-present dark families have identical median site occupancy in the longest stratum (>=250 residues: 27 versus 27 sites; 57 versus 54 samples, an informative negative result showing that for full-length proteins, global reference absence is not driven by low local occupancy), whereas in the shortest stratum (<60 residues) reference-present families occupy more sites (50 versus 44 sites; 230 versus 151 samples).

Hypothesis 4 (Rank 4, Exploratory; requires a lightweight script on IBEX-pinned inputs): Operon neighborhood and co-directionalannotated anchor analysis for the 1,031 confidence-qualified structurally unaligned dark families ( versus the 1,807 fold-matched dark families).
- Exploratory/confirmatory status and companion-paper boundary: Exploratory post hoc genomic-context analysis for Section 2.5; strictly restricted to cellular chromosomal/plasmid contigs in the 5,438 species representatives (excluding viral/phage contigs or viral hallmark neighborhoods covered in ../empty-quarter-phages).
- Scientific question: Do the 1,031 confidence-qualified dark families that lack a reference fold (qTM < 0.5) reside within conserved, co-directional operonic neighborhoods alongside functionally annotated genes (for example, ABC transporters, two-component sensors, radiation/desiccation repair, or compatible-solute synthesis pathways) at the same rate as the 1,807 dark families that match a known fold (qTM >= 0.5), or are they enriched on short, isolated or lineage-restricted contigs?
- Why it adds substantive value: For the 1,031 structurally novel dark family candidates (and especially the 136 priority targets that are both confident at pLDDT >= 0.70, qTM < 0.5 and detected in metatranscriptomes), sequence and structure homology searches reach a dead end by definition. In prokaryotic genomics, conserved synteny and operonic co-directionality (intergenic distance <= 50 bp on the same strand across >= 2 species representatives) provide an orthogonal, sequence-homology-independent line of evidence for biological function and against sporadic overprediction.
- Actual available inputs (distinguishing local versus IBEX-pinned paths):
  Locally available: reproducibility/darkmatter/inputs/04_structure/00_structure_clean/05_validate/per_rep_structures.tsv.gz (identifies the 2,838 confidence-qualified dark families, their qTM/alnTM scores, and family IDs).
  IBEX-pinned inputs (verified in reproducibility/darkmatter/upstream_code/06_darkmatter/darkfam_basis_clean/README.md and 04_structure/pfam_candidates_clean/README.md; not stored in full in the local workspace): (i) per-contig Prodigal GFF3/FAA coordinates for the 14,426 bins / 5,438 representatives (/ibex/project/c2188/empty-quarter/06_darkmatter/darkfam_basis_clean/ and catalogue gene tables); (ii) Bakta/eggNOG/KEGG functional annotations of flanking CDSs on the same contigs; and (iii) family membership mapping for the 2,838 folded families (reproducibility/darkmatter/upstream_code/04_structure/pfam_candidates_clean/ uses candidate_members.faa and QnotK_reps.faa on IBEX).
- Unit of replication and estimand: The unit of replication is the confidence-qualified dark family (1,031 K_reps with qTM < 0.5 versus 1,807 QnotK_reps with qTM >= 0.5). Restricting to member genes located on contigs with at least 3 called CDSs (not at a contig edge), the primary estimands are: (i) the proportion of families in which >= 50% of member genes sit within <= 50 bp same-strand intergenic distance of a functionally annotated (UniRef50/KEGG-positive) neighbor; and (ii) the family-level neighborhood conservation score (proportion of member genomes sharing the same flanking KEGG orthologue or Pfam clan within +/- 2 CDS positions).
- Controls and dependence structure: Compare the 1,031 K_reps against the 1,807 QnotK_reps stratified by host phylum (Actinomycetota, Thermoplasmatota, Chloroflexota, etc.) and contig length (log10 contig bp) using a stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test or logistic regression with phylum fixed effects.
- Outcome interpretation (including informative negative result): If K_reps exhibit high co-directional operonic embedding with annotated neighbors comparable to QnotK_reps (for example, >= 60% in tight co-directional operons with conserved KEGG neighbors across multiple species), this provides strong independent evidence that the 1,031 low-qTM families are integrated components of cellular pathways and yields immediate functional guilt-by-association hypotheses for the 136 expressed priority targets. Conversely, an informative negative result (if K_reps are significantly depleted in conserved annotated flanking neighbors or enriched at contig boundaries/unannotated gene cassettes even after controlling for contig length) would indicate that structurally unaligned dark families cluster in hypervariable genomic islands or mobile accessory regions rather than housekeeping operons.
